root_cause.text: The `rxe_rcv` function in the Soft RoCE driver validates the incoming packet length only against the fixed header size, allowing an integer underflow to occur in `payload_size()` when subtracting the BTH pad and ICRC size from a short packet.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces the check `unlikely(skb->len < header_size(pkt))` with `unlikely(pkt->paylen < header_size(pkt) + bth_pad(pkt) + RXE_ICRC_SIZE)` in `rxe_recv.c` to ensure the packet is large enough to prevent `payload_size()` from underflowing.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `rxe_rcv` validates the packet length using `if (unlikely(skb->len < header_size(pkt))) goto drop;` on line 386. This only ensures that the packet is large enough to contain the header. However, later on line 396, it calls `payload_size(pkt)` which subtracts the header size, padding, and ICRC size (`RXE_ICRC_SIZE`) from the packet length. If the packet length is greater than `header_size(pkt)` but less than `header_size(pkt) + RXE_ICRC_SIZE`, an integer underflow will occur in `payload_size(pkt)`, leading to an out-of-bounds read in `crc32_le`.
